Reference - Authors: A Darji; K Niebuhr; M Hense; J Wehland; T Chakraborty; S Weiss
Reference - Title: Neutralizing monoclonal antibodies against listeriolysin: mapping of epitopes involved in pore formation.
Epitope - Molecule Parent: Listeriolysin O
Immunization - Comments: Monoclonal antibodies were generated against formaldehyde-treated, concentrated culture supernatant derived from Listeria monocytogenes EGD.
Assay - Comments: The assay investigated the ability of the monoclonal antibody to neutralize the hemolytic activity of listeriolysin by incubation with listeriolysin, adding sheep erythrocytes, and measuring the  amount of hemoglobin released.  The neutralization activity was reported as strong.  To distinguish whether the neutralizing antibody inhibited binding of listeriolysin to the cellular membrane or a subsequent step, the monoclonal antibody was preincubated with listeriolysin at neutralizing concentrations and this complex was incubated with the mouse fibrblast cell line, 36.2.1.  It was shown that while hemolytic activity was inhibited, the monoclonal antibody was able to bind to the fibroblasts via listeriolysin, suggesting that neutralization was not mediated by binding of listeriolysin to the cellular membrane.

Epitope - Molecule Parent: Major outer membrane porin, serovar D
Epitope - Comments: The author has confirmed that this epitope is as indicated in the reference Conlan, JW et al. (1989) J Gen Microbiol 135:3219 [PMID: 2483992] and the cited reference Stagg AJ et al. (1993) Immunology 79:1 [PMID: 8099564]. The precursor protein described in the database includes a 22 amino acid signal sequence, whereas the amino acid positions in the references refer to the mature protein.
1st in vivo Process - Process Type: Administration in vivo to prevent or reduce disease
1st immunogen - Source Molecule: Major outer membrane porin, serovar L1 precursor (MOMP)

Five of eight epitope immunized mice had less severe salpingitis than unvaccinated mice. In mice receiving four doses of peptide, three of 6 mice had less severe disease.Balb/c mice were also protected by epitope immunization.

Assay - Comments: The epitope was able to inhibit binding of the monoclonal antibody to C. trachomatis L2 DnaK. Exchange of each of the next three amino acids with alanine reduced the specificity of the peptides (60 to 70% inhibition). Epitope - Source Molecule: Major outer membrane porin, serovar D

1st immunogen - Name: Chlamydia trachomatis D/UW-3/CX (Chlamydia trachomatis str. D/UW-3/CX)
1st immunogen - Reference Name: C. trachomatis serovar D elementary bodies (EB)

2nd immunogen - Name: Major outer membrane porin, serovar D
